title: Word Parts: Roots, Prefixes, Suffixes
body:
## How to decode any term in five lines

1. **Read the suffix first.** It tells you what *kind* of word this is: a condition, a procedure, a measurement.
2. **Read the prefix.** It modifies: how much, where, when, which side.
3. **Read the root last.** It names the body part or substance.
4. **Assemble back to front:** suffix, then prefix, then root.
5. **Sanity-check it against the patient.** If the assembled meaning does not describe something a body can actually do, you split the word wrong.

Worked example: `peri-card-itis` gives inflammation (`-itis`), around (`peri-`), the heart (`cardi`) — inflammation of the sac around the heart.

## Roots

| Root | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `cardi/o` | Heart | cardiology |
| `angi/o` | Vessel | angiogram |
| `vas/o`, `vascul/o` | Vessel, duct | vasodilation |
| `arteri/o` | Artery | arteriosclerosis |
| `phleb/o`, `ven/o` | Vein | phlebotomy |
| `hem/o`, `hemat/o` | Blood | hematoma |
| `my/o` | Muscle | myocardium |
| `oste/o` | Bone | osteoporosis |
| `arthr/o` | Joint | arthritis |
| `chondr/o` | Cartilage | chondromalacia |
| `myel/o` | Bone marrow, spinal cord | myelogram |
| `neur/o` | Nerve | neuropathy |
| `encephal/o` | Brain | encephalitis |
| `cerebr/o` | Cerebrum | cerebral |
| `mening/o` | Membranes covering the brain and cord | meningitis |
| `pneum/o`, `pneumon/o` | Lung, air | pneumothorax |
| `pulmon/o` | Lung | pulmonary |
| `bronch/o` | Bronchus | bronchitis |
| `trache/o` | Trachea | tracheostomy |
| `laryng/o` | Voice box | laryngitis |
| `pharyng/o` | Throat | pharyngitis |
| `rhin/o`, `nas/o` | Nose | rhinorrhea |
| `thorac/o` | Chest | thoracotomy |
| `pleur/o` | Lining of the lung | pleurisy |
| `gastr/o` | Stomach | gastritis |
| `enter/o` | Small intestine | enteritis |
| `col/o`, `colon/o` | Colon | colonoscopy |
| `esophag/o` | Esophagus | esophagitis |
| `hepat/o` | Liver | hepatitis |
| `chol/e`, `cholecyst/o` | Bile, gallbladder | cholecystitis |
| `pancreat/o` | Pancreas | pancreatitis |
| `nephr/o`, `ren/o` | Kidney | nephrology, renal |
| `cyst/o` | Bladder, sac | cystitis |
| `ur/o` | Urine, urinary tract | urology |
| `hyster/o`, `metr/o` | Uterus | hysterectomy |
| `oophor/o` | Ovary | oophorectomy |
| `salping/o` | Fallopian tube | salpingitis |
| `orchi/o` | Testis | orchitis |
| `derm/o`, `dermat/o` | Skin | dermatitis |
| `cutane/o` | Skin | subcutaneous |
| `aden/o` | Gland | adenopathy |
| `lymph/o` | Lymph | lymphadenopathy |
| `splen/o` | Spleen | splenectomy |
| `ophthalm/o`, `ocul/o` | Eye | ophthalmoscope |
| `ot/o` | Ear | otitis |
| `gluc/o`, `glyc/o` | Sugar | hypoglycemia |
| `cyt/o` | Cell | cytology |
| `path/o` | Disease | pathology |
| `therm/o` | Heat | hyperthermia |
| `phag/o` | Eat, swallow | dysphagia |

## Prefixes

| Prefix | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `a-`, `an-` | Without, absent | apnea |
| `anti-` | Against | antibiotic |
| `brady-` | Slow | bradycardia |
| `tachy-` | Fast | tachycardia |
| `dys-` | Painful, difficult, abnormal | dyspnea |
| `eu-` | Good, normal | eupnea |
| `hyper-` | Above normal, excessive | hypertension |
| `hypo-` | Below normal, deficient | hypoxia |
| `peri-` | Around | pericardium |
| `endo-` | Within, inside | endotracheal |
| `epi-` | Upon, over | epidermis |
| `intra-` | Within | intramuscular |
| `inter-` | Between | intercostal |
| `sub-` | Under, below | sublingual |
| `supra-` | Above | supraventricular |
| `trans-` | Across, through | transdermal |
| `post-` | After | postictal |
| `pre-`, `pro-` | Before, in front of | prenatal |
| `poly-` | Many, much | polyuria |
| `oligo-` | Few, scanty | oliguria |
| `hemi-` | Half | hemiplegia |
| `bi-` | Two, both | bilateral |
| `uni-` | One | unilateral |
| `macro-` | Large | macrocytic |
| `micro-` | Small | microcephaly |
| `neo-` | New | neonate |
| `pan-` | All | pancytopenia |

## Suffixes

| Suffix | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `-algia`, `-dynia` | Pain | myalgia |
| `-emia` | Blood condition | anemia |
| `-itis` | Inflammation | appendicitis |
| `-osis` | Abnormal condition | cyanosis |
| `-oma` | Tumor, mass, swelling | hematoma |
| `-pathy` | Disease | neuropathy |
| `-ectomy` | Surgical removal | appendectomy |
| `-otomy` | Cutting into | tracheotomy |
| `-ostomy` | Creating a permanent opening | colostomy |
| `-plasty` | Surgical repair | angioplasty |
| `-pexy` | Surgical fixation | nephropexy |
| `-rrhaphy` | Suturing | herniorrhaphy |
| `-scopy` | Looking inside | colonoscopy |
| `-gram` | The record or image | electrocardiogram |
| `-graphy` | The process of recording | radiography |
| `-meter` | Measuring device | thermometer |
| `-pnea` | Breathing | apnea |
| `-plegia` | Paralysis | hemiplegia |
| `-paresis` | Partial weakness | hemiparesis |
| `-rrhage`, `-rrhagia` | Bursting forth, bleeding | hemorrhage |
| `-rrhea` | Flow, discharge | rhinorrhea |
| `-uria` | Urine condition | hematuria |
| `-penia` | Deficiency | thrombocytopenia |
| `-cytosis` | Increase in cells | leukocytosis |
| `-megaly` | Enlargement | cardiomegaly |
| `-sclerosis` | Hardening | atherosclerosis |
| `-stenosis` | Narrowing | aortic stenosis |
| `-lysis` | Breakdown, destruction | hemolysis |
| `-emesis` | Vomiting | hematemesis |
| `-phasia` | Speech | aphasia |
| `-phagia` | Swallowing | dysphagia |
| `-esthesia` | Sensation | anesthesia |

> **Trap:** `-otomy` is a cut you close. `-ostomy` is an opening you leave. One letter separates a tracheotomy from a permanent tracheostomy.

## Directional and positional terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Anatomic position | Standing, facing forward, arms at sides, palms forward |
| Anterior (ventral) / posterior (dorsal) | Front / back |
| Superior (cephalad) / inferior (caudad) | Toward the head / toward the feet |
| Medial / lateral | Toward the midline / away from the midline |
| Proximal / distal | Closer to / farther from the trunk or point of attachment |
| Superficial / deep | Near the surface / away from the surface |
| Unilateral / bilateral | One side / both sides |
| Ipsilateral / contralateral | Same side / opposite side |
| Supine / prone | Face up / face down |
| Fowler's | Sitting up `60–90` degrees; semi-Fowler's `30–45`; high Fowler's `90` |
| Trendelenburg | Flat with the feet elevated; reverse Trendelenburg is head up |
| Left lateral recumbent | On the left side — the recovery position, and the position for a pregnant patient |
| Midclavicular / midaxillary line | Vertical reference lines used for `V4` and chest decompression |
| Flexion / extension | Bending / straightening a joint |
| Abduction / adduction | Moving away from / toward the midline |
| Supination / pronation | Palm up / palm down |
| Dorsiflexion / plantarflexion | Toes up / toes down |
